findings.detail: The worktree modifies the manifested file tests/advanced-oracle.test.js (new AT-LF-24 executePlan assertions) but leaves its manifest line `6997a0be…  tests/advanced-oracle.test.js` untouched, while the manifest lines for scripts/check-advanced-spec.js and tests/helpers/advanced.js were regenerated and gate1.sig was re-signed in this same worktree. Under AD-28 the verifier recomputes every manifested digest before any code test, so on these exact bytes the armed gate either fails closed (npm test cannot be green, and §12.3 blocker 6 is unmet) or the manifest+signature were regenerated after the oracle bytes moved — which is the implementation context moving its own bar, the precise scenario AT-GATE-2 exists to refuse. Release requires the key holder re-signing the final bytes and a recorded gate run; I could not execute the verifier in this session to distinguish the two cases.

findings.anchor: rig/lib/lint-format.js:777 runAutofix; technical-spec §9.4 "All five guarantees are now implemented; the shell-trust suite is closed"
findings.detail: runAutofix executes the repository's own fix command and its verify command via bare `spawnTask(cmd.argv, { cwd: target })`. Unlike runGrade and runReadOnly it applies no networkIsolationPrefix (so an approved fix command has unconditional outbound reachability, contrary to AT-LF-22/D28 guarantee 3, which is scoped to 'every repository-owned task Rig executes') and passes no timeoutMs/memoryLimitMb (so AT-LF-23/D28 guarantee 4 produces no distinct killed-and-reported state — a runaway autofix simply hangs). It is also a mutating action, i.e. the highest-consequence of the three execution seams. No test exercises isolation or caps on this path; the only autofix coverage is the approval/verification assertion in tests/advanced-oracle.test.js:828. The technical specification's claim that the shell-trust suite is closed is contradicted by this seam.

No shipped service binding declares a `network` field (grep for '"network"' under rig/catalog/services returns nothing), so every check command the installed .rig/bin/check.js runs today takes the 'undeclared' branch: no isolation, plus a console.warn on every CI run. AD-39 sanctions this as a temporary compatibility state, so it is not a contract violation, but it means the default-deny isolation code in the shipping CI path is exercised only by synthetic bindings in tests/guarantee-coverage.test.js AT-CAP-3 and is dead for real users, while the CI log gains a warning line per check. Worth naming as an explicit debt rather than leaving it to read as enforced.

resolveRecordPath/containedPath now run over every journal record up front, and classifiedRel throws `repository path escapes target` on an escaping record. A journal containing one such record therefore aborts uninstall with an exception instead of naming that file best-effort and removing everything else, which is the reporting shape AT-UNINSTALL-2 asks for. It is fail-closed and happens before any mutation, so nothing is damaged, but a user with one bad record gets a stack trace rather than a removal report naming the offending path.
